audit_findings: The initial Fortran material literals have default-real precision before assignment to real64. Read decimal parameters directly from the authoritative JSON through real64 namelist input instead.
The initial executable implements only dt=0.01; preregistered dt=0.005 was missing.
Exit code zero alone did not test finite accepted state, complete history cardinality or the preregistered water ledger.
Centisecond process timing without a same-job Richards reference cannot establish the requested speed comparison.
The initial workflow had no aggregate or numerical refinement analysis. Original queued screen runs are not qualification authority.
semantic_binding: P3 implemented HOLD is prescribed bottom flux k0 (Python None; Richards bottom_mode=2), not prescribed head psi0. P4 preserves that implemented boundary condition. These controlled histories are not meteorological, seasonal or a MODFLOW coupling benchmark.

equation_conformance.test: Compare psi, K, dtheta/dt and both boundary fluxes with the pinned Python equations at uniform and nonuniform states in both histories and all forcing phases.
equation_conformance.invalid_domain: Reject input Se outside (0,1); no clipping or fallback.

completion_gate: Two histories with 60 unique daily states each; all layer states finite and in the original qualified domain; cumulative ledger <=1e-8 cm checked before every accepted substep; expected RHS count = 4*60/dt per history.
refinement: Report full-versus-half discrepancies and their ratios to full-versus-R128 error for each P3 metric separately. No new absolute application gate. A half-step success does not retroactively qualify a failed primary dt=0.01 candidate.

timing.wall: Python perf_counter around each subprocess with output redirected to a file; identical runner and workflow, interleaved candidate, half-step and R128 calls; compilation excluded.
timing.cpu: Child process user+system CPU via resource.getrusage; also retain Fortran internal CPU and wall timer.
timing.output_semantics: Process comparison includes each harness's own output and orchestration. It is not a pure hydraulic-kernel speedup.
timing.failed_runs: Retain elapsed time and diagnostics as failure overhead, never as successful speedup.

interpretation_limits: Compilation and integrator both change relative to Python Heun; a successful RK4 test cannot uniquely attribute gains to compilation alone.
Fixed-step failure supports a limitation of that tested numerical policy, not impossibility of integrating the frozen equations.
R128 and R64 are controlled Richards harnesses, not end-to-end Full SWAP application workflows.
B05/B16 forcing was already exposed in P3; this is frozen-panel numerical revalidation, not a fresh hydrological blind test.
